question.problem:
The matrix $S$ is given below. Let ${s}_{1}$, ${s}_{2}$,  ${s}_{3}$ and ${s}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $S.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{s}_{1},{s}_{2},{s}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(S).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${s}_{4}={x}_{1}{s}_{1}+{x}_{2}{s}_{2}+{x}_{3}{s}_{3}.$ 

$$
S=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ -2 & -1 & 10 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $S$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ -2 & -1 & 10 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9 \\ -1 & -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(S)$ is $\{{s}_{1},{s}_{2}\}.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that $B=\{{s}_{1},{s}_{2},{s}_{3}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(S).$
